summary: Dashboard at http://<ip>:3001 showed 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred' because the production env var NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_URL contained a trailing 'n' (http://<ip>:3000n).
user_visible_impact: Full white-screen crash of the trading dashboard on load; no live data rendered.
root_cause: web/.env.production on the VPS was written with a trailing 'n' character in the value: NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_URL=http://<ip>:3000n. Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars at build time, so the string 'http://<ip>:3000n' was baked into the client chunk. At runtime, new EventSource(`${SSE_URL}/events`) is constructed with an invalid port ('3000n'), which throws. The throw occurred inside useFeed's useEffect during client hydration, which React/Next.js surfaces as the generic 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred' page.
what_went_wrong: An environment file value was written without validating the resulting URL. The trailing stray character was not caught because the build still succeeded (it is a runtime, not build-time, failure) and no headless/browser smoke test was run on the initial deploy. Verification relied on HTTP 200 + chunk 200 checks, which cannot detect a client-side runtime exception.
contributing_factors: No client Error Boundary existed, so the real error message was hidden behind Next.js's generic 'Application error' text.
Deploy verification was limited to HTTP status codes and asset 200s; no browser-level execution check.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* inlining means a bad env value silently ships into the bundle.
corrective_action_taken: Corrected .env.production to NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_URL=http://<ip>:3000 and rebuilt remotely.
Hardened useFeed.ts: EventSource construction wrapped in try/catch with backoff retry so a bad URL degrades to 'disconnected' rather than crashing the app.
Added app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx to surface real error messages instead of the generic crash page.
Re-verified with a headless Chrome CDP run capturing exceptions and console errors.
preventive_action: Add a browser-level (headless CDP/Playwright) smoke check to the deploy checklist so client-side runtime exceptions are caught, and validate env-derived URLs before/after build.
